text:
marta: FYI pushed a prototype for a per-tenant sampling feedback loop to feat/tenant-sampling. Trying to capture tail traces for tenants that are degrading while keeping head sampling aggressive for cheap requests.

devon: Nice. Quick Q — how do you plan to avoid thrashing sampling rates for noisy tenants?

marta: Good call. The prototype keeps a short-term error budget per-tenant (5m window) and only adjusts sampling when the tail-error exceed threshold + a stability multiplier. Also we rate-limit adjustments to once per 10m.

ali: Can you paste the config snippet? Want to see how it maps to routes/tiers.

marta: Sure:
```
# per-tenant sampling config (yaml)
tenants: 
  tenant_id: 
    base_head_rate: 0.75
    base_tail_rate: 0.01
    max_tail_rate: 0.5
    error_threshold: 0.02
    adjust_cooldown_seconds: 600
    stability_multiplier: 1.5
routes: 
  "/api/generate": { path_priority: high, tier_sensitive: true }
```

sam: Where does this live in the pipeline? Before or after the OTLP exporter? We need to be careful w/ span attributes used for tenant routing.

marta: It runs in the ingest worker before exporting. We use tenant and route tags from the span resource. If route tag missing we fallback to route heuristics. Then we mark spans with `sampled: true|false` and a `sampling_reason` attribute.

devon: What about duplicate spans & tombstones? If we re-sample after the fact we might create duplicates downstream.

marta: We add a tombstone header for dropped spans so downstream exporters (and our retention tiering) can dedupe. The idea: tombstone entries are cheap markers that say "we intentionally dropped X at T" so replays don't inflate metrics. ingest-bot will emit a small metric for tombstones so ops can monitor.

ingest-bot: tombstone-counter incremented tenant=alpha route=/api/generate amount=23

ali: How will this show up in Console? We should expose per-tenant sampling rates + recent adjustments + a small timeline for the last 24h so support can answer "why did my traces drop".

marta: Agreed. Plan: wire metrics into the telemetry dashboard -> per-tenant panel, history of head/tail rates, and an explanation card (why we adjusted). Also a fallback toggle to pin a tenant at a fixed sampling.

sam: Two operational concerns: 1) cost spikes when we bump tail rate for large tenants, 2) edge-case where a tenant toggles a high-traffic route that suddenly forces us to allocate more tail capture and we hit exporter/retention limits.

devon: For (1) we can set a soft budget (tokens per minute) per-tenant. If bump would exceed budget we instead queue a gradual ramp and notify the tenant owner in Console.

ali: For (2) recommend a global circuit-breaker: if total tail tokens in 1m > threshold we fall back to cohort-level tail capture (e.g., only capture for customers in the incident cohort) and emit an incident alert to eng-sre.

marta: Implemented a simplified sim in the branch: a replay tool that feeds synthetic load and checks budgets across tenants. Results look sane for our staging-scale.

sam: Can we include a simple back-of-envelope estimate for token costs when tail rate moves from 1% to 25% for a 500 rps tenant? Ops needs numbers for cost alerts.

marta: Will add a calc to the PR description. Roughly: 500 rps * 60s * 0.25 ~ 7500 traces/min. Multiply by avg tokens-per-trace (we use 120 tokens) and unit cost -> big jump. I'll put exact numbers.

devon: One more thought — this relies on reliable tenant attribution on spans. We should add a validation job that surface spans with missing or inconsistent tenant tags and surface to Console daily.

ali: Agreed. Otherwise we bias sampling. Also add tests for path heuristics fallback.

marta: Plan: finish unit tests, add console panels, add cost calc in PR, and ship to staging behind a feature flag. Asking for quick reviews from @devon @ali @sam.

devon: I'll review tonight. Look closely at cooldown logic.

ali: I'll follow up on dashboard mocks.

sam: I'll run exporter load test against staging and watch tombstone metrics.

marta: Thanks all. If anyone hits blockers ping me. :rocket:
